cues.en: Well, you seem to like the jacket, so I'll keep it. I have a bit of a fascination with stoplights, or traffic lights, if you prefer. They boil down to remarkably simple devices, little more than indicators. But thanks to drivers' education and the magic of the human brain, they are remarkably effective at safely controlling traffic at intersections. Most of the time. Now, there's so much to get into regarding traffic lights. Traffic engineering is a fascinating subject which I don't feel qualified to discuss, but there's quite the rabbit hole to fall into.
cues.zh: 大家好像挺喜欢这件夹克，那我就继续穿着了。我对红绿灯，或者说交通信号灯，一直有种特别的着迷。它们本质上是非常简单的装置，无非就是几个指示灯而已。但多亏了驾校培训和人类大脑的神奇运作，它们在十字路口安全管制交通方面极其有效。大多数时候是这样。关于交通信号灯，能聊的可太多了。交通工程学是一门引人入胜的学科，虽然我觉得自己还没资格去深谈，但这绝对是个让人深陷其中的话题。

cues.en: This video is about a simple but groundbreaking innovation in the traffic light and the lessons it can tell us about innovation in general. This is about the LED traffic light and the caution of, but sometimes. I live in an area of my town that's not terribly well traveled. Though there are many four-lane roads with speed limits of 35 to 40 miles an hour, the traffic volume honestly doesn't often justify having two lanes in each direction.
cues.zh: 本期视频要讲的是交通信号灯上一项简单却具有开创性的创新，以及它能给普通创新带来的启示。我们要聊的是 LED 交通信号灯，以及“但是，凡事总有例外”这句警示。我住在镇上一个人流车流都不太多的区域。尽管这里有很多限速 35 到 40 英里的四车道马路，但讲真，这车流量往往用不着双向四车道。

cues.en: Many of the stoplights in this area have been neglected and are still using good old fashioned incandescent bulbs with colored glass lenses. Actually, some are so old that they still have the written text walk and don't walk in their pedestrian signals and there are even a few that use the old 8 inch lenses for the green and yellow lights with only the important red light getting a full 12 inch lens. Granted, these stoplights have had their control systems upgraded over the years.
cues.zh: 这片区域的很多交通灯年久失修，还在使用老式的有色玻璃透镜白炽灯泡。实际上，有些灯甚至老旧到行人信号灯上还写着“走”和“不要走”的文字，甚至还有少数绿灯和黄灯用的是老式8英寸透镜，只有关键的红灯才配有完整的12英寸透镜。当然，这些交通灯的控制系统多年来还是升级过的。

cues.en: There are vehicle presence detectors embedded in the road surface to alter their timing and behavior, and they are equipped with photocells to detect the tuned strobe light on emergency vehicles and stop traffic in opposing directions.
cues.zh: 路面下埋设了车辆感应器来调整配时和运行逻辑，它们还配备了光敏元件，用来检测应急车辆上的特定频闪灯，从而阻断对向车流。

cues.en: and some have even had countdown timers added to the pedestrian signals. But the fixtures themselves have remained mostly unchanged. They are still the same incandescent traffic lights that may very well have been in place for a good number of decades. I should add that vehicle presence detection has been around long before the LED traffic light and it's very likely that these intersections have the same control equipment they've always had. But in any case, the fact that they are still using incandescent lamp technology is a little odd.
cues.zh: 有些甚至在行人信号灯上加装了倒计时器。但灯具本身基本没怎么变。它们依然是那些白炽灯交通信号灯，很可能已经在那儿立了好几十年了。另外我想补充的是，车辆检测技术早在 LED 交通信号灯出现前就有了，而且这些路口极有可能一直沿用着原有的控制设备。但不管怎样，它们至今仍在使用白炽灯技术，确实有点奇怪。

cues.en: Setting aside the nostalgic or aesthetic reasons to prefer an incandescent stoplight, I'll admit the fade-in fade-out as each light changes states is charming, the LED traffic light is just objectively better in nearly every respect. For example, incandescent stoplight fixtures, because they are designed to be opened to replace the bulb, typically get dirty on the inside over time. And it seems the technicians who replace the lamps often don't seem bothered to clean the lenses or reflectors.
cues.zh: 抛开对白炽灯信号灯的情怀或审美偏好不谈——我承认每次变灯时那种渐亮渐灭的效果确实很有魅力——LED 交通信号灯在几乎各个方面都客观上更为优越。例如，白炽灯信号灯具因为要开盖更换灯泡，内部通常会随着时间的推移变脏。而且负责换灯的技术人员似乎经常懒得去清理透镜或反光罩。

cues.en: This leads to many lights with a dull appearance that's hard to see in bright sunlight. This obviously isn't great, and is actually kind of dangerous, but whatever. The LED light, on the other hand, is completely sealed. In fact, here's an LED traffic light module. Yes, they really are this big, they just seem much smaller when they're grandstanding on their pedestals or hanging up high in the air. These are designed with the ability to replace the lenses in existing incandescent lights and function as a retrofit device, as well as simply be the default standard for new traffic light installations.
cues.zh: 这导致许多信号灯外观暗淡，在强烈的阳光下很难看清。这显然不太好，甚至可以说有点危险，但也只能这样了。而 LED 灯则是完全密封的。实际上，我这里就有一个 LED 交通信号灯模块。是的，它们真的有这么大，只是立在高高的柱子上或挂在高空时显得小得多。它们既可以替换现有白炽灯里的透镜，作为改造装置使用，也是新建交通信号灯的默认标准。

cues.en: Because the entire module is replaced if needed, it can be completely sealed. LED lights thus don't end up looking like that. These LED modules use about a tenth the energy of the incandescent lights they replace, which is not only great for energy savings, but it means battery backups for the lighting control system can keep the intersection controlled for hours even during a blackout. And of course, they last so much longer than the light bulbs in an old-fashioned fixture do.
cues.zh: 因为需要时会替换整个模块，所以它可以做到完全密封。这样一来，LED 灯就不会变成那副模样。这些 LED 模块消耗的电量大约只有被替换白炽灯的十分之一，这不仅非常节能，还意味着即使发生停电，照明控制系统的备用电池也能维持路口控制好几个小时。当然，它们的使用寿命也比老式灯具里的灯泡长得多。

cues.en: This 116 watt light from Sylvania only lasts 8,000 hours, which may seem like a lot, but assuming a roughly 50-50 on time for green and red, that won't even cover two years. And since pretty much every intersection has at least two lights visible in each direction, there's a total of at least 16 of these bad boys in a very small intersection, not including yellow. This would mean that a light will go out about every two months. And let me tell you, that's remarkably in line with how often I see a light go out at any given intersection.
cues.zh: Sylvania 这款 116 瓦的灯泡寿命只有 8000 小时，看似挺长，但假设红绿灯各亮一半时间，它连两年都撑不到。而且几乎每个路口每个方向都至少能看到两盏灯，哪怕是很小的路口，不算黄灯也至少有 16 个这玩意儿。这意味着大约每两个月就得坏一盏。老实说，这跟我平时在路口看到红绿灯坏掉的频率完全对得上。

cues.en: In fact, on the day I left to start taking photos of the stoplights around me like the big old dork that I am, this light burnt out. Granted, there are two other lights providing redundancy, but they're also really dirty and hard to see anyway. I went out again a few days later to take some photos I had forgotten to take, and now this light is also out. What fun! At this one intersection
cues.zh: 事实上，就在我像个超级大宅男一样，跑出门去拍周围红绿灯的那天，这盏灯就烧坏了。虽然另外还有两盏灯作为备用，但它们也特别脏，本来就很难看清。几天后我为了补拍几张忘了拍的照片又去了一趟，结果这盏灯也灭了。真有意思！光是这一个路口，

cues.en: including all arrows, pedestrian signals, and standard orb indicators, there are 94 lights just waiting to burn out. Conversely, you almost never see an LED stoplight with a signal that's out. They last so long that it's a very rare occurrence. It does happen, it's not like they last forever. But even when they do fail, some designs don't even fail all at once, with this module still mostly functional save for some dead diodes. In the past two years, I've only seen one LED light completely fail anywhere.
cues.zh: 算上所有箭头灯、行人过街信号灯和普通的圆形指示灯，就有整整 94 盏灯随时可能烧坏。相反，你几乎从来见不到哪个 LED 红绿灯是不亮的。它们寿命极长，坏掉的情况非常少见。当然坏还是会坏的，毕竟不可能永远不坏。但就算坏了，有些设计也不会直接全灭，比如这个模块，除了一些坏掉的二极管，大部分其实还能正常工作。过去两年里，我总共就见过一次 LED 灯彻底坏掉的情况。

cues.en: whereas I've seen about a dozen lights go out just in my neighborhood. Now, I can't tell you why my local streets and sanitation department, or whatever agency is tasked with maintaining these specific traffic controls, hasn't invested in retrofitting these stoplights with LED replacements. They're just an odd holdout, I guess, or perhaps they think it's cheaper to just do things as they are.
cues.zh: 而光是在我住的街区，我就见过大概有十来盏灯熄灭了。我也搞不懂为什么我们当地的环卫部门，或者负责维护这些特定交通管制的机构，没有出资把这些红绿灯改造成 LED 的。我猜他们可能只是个死守旧例的奇葩，又或者他们觉得维持现状成本更低。

cues.en: News flash, it isn't, because if these lights do use 116 watt bulbs, then with pedestrian signals included, at any given time the intersection is using around a kilowatt and a half or more. Meaning it costs about $3.60 to operate daily, assuming average rates in Illinois.
cues.zh: 事实并非如此，因为如果这些信号灯确实用的是 116 瓦的灯泡，再加上行人信号灯，那么在任意时刻，这个路口都要消耗大约 1.5 千瓦甚至更多的电量。按伊利诺伊州的平均电费来算，这意味着每天的运行成本约为 3.6 美元。

cues.en: Add to that the cost of relamping the fixtures every two years, or far more likely the reactionary maintenance when a lamp fails multiple times during a year, and it seems really foolish to still be using these lights as they are, especially because these modules typically end up on eBay or elsewhere for about $10 each. I don't know how much they cost new from the manufacturer, but I can't imagine they're terribly expensive. But when the LED's stoplight first made its way onto the scene, one of its central advantages became a disadvantage.
cues.zh: 再加上每两年更换一次灯泡的费用——或者更有可能的是，在一年内灯泡坏了好几次时进行的被动维修成本——继续按原样使用这些灯就显得非常愚蠢了，尤其是这些模块在 eBay 或其他地方通常只要 10 美元左右一个。我不知道直接从厂家买全新的要多少钱，但想必也不会太贵。然而，当 LED 红绿灯最初登场时，它的核心优势之一却反倒成了一项劣势。

cues.en: See, because the good ol' incandescent bulb is so terribly inefficient, it spews a lot of heat out all sides and kept the fixtures toasty warm. This had the lovely side effect of keeping snow and ice from building up on them in cold climates. Many municipalities started discovering that their new LED fixtures, which are 10 times more efficient and thus release just 10% of the heat, didn't do that. In bad snowstorms with high winds, it is very possible for the snow to make its way past the visor and stick to the face of the stoplight.
cues.zh: 你看，因为老式白炽灯效率实在太低，会向四周散发大量热量，让灯具始终保持温热。在寒冷气候下，这带来了一个极好的附带效果，就是防止积雪和结冰。许多地方政府开始发现，他们换上的全新 LED 灯具做不到这一点，因为 LED 效率高了十倍，散发的热量只有原来的十分之一。在强风暴雪天气下，雪很有可能会越过遮光罩，直接糊在交通信号灯表面。

cues.en: Not producing enough heat to melt the snow, the LED stoplight might become impossible to see in this scenario. This caused quite a few accidents, some of which were regrettably fatal. However, if the drivers at fault remembered their driver's education, a stoplight that isn't indicating should be treated as a stop sign, turning the intersection into an always stop. But people are stupid, so accidents happen.
cues.zh: 由于热量不足以融化积雪，这种情况下可能完全看不清 LED 信号灯。这引发了相当多的交通事故，其中一些甚至不幸致命。然而，如果肇事司机还记得驾校教的内容，不显示的信号灯应当作停车标志处理，路口会自动变成全向停车。但人总会犯蠢，事故就这么发生了。

cues.en: As you may imagine, the news reports started flooding in. Energy efficient stoplights cause accidents. These new LED stoplights can't melt snow. The Green Revolution knows no bounds. Cold traffic lights leave drivers confused. Etc. Etc. The really stupid articles pointed out that while a solution might be possible, it would eat into the energy savings presented by the LEDs.
cues.zh: 不出所料，新闻报道铺天盖地而来。节能红绿灯引发交通事故。新型 LED 红绿灯无法融雪。绿色革命毫无节制。冰冷的交通信号灯让司机摸不着头脑。等等，等等。那些极其愚蠢的文章甚至指出，虽然可能有解决方案，但这会抵消 LED 带来的节能效果。

cues.en: That is a really dumb argument as we'll discuss momentarily. I even recall a news report when I was younger suggesting that a heated surface would use more energy than an incandescent traffic light, so really, what's the point? This is the danger of but sometimes. It goes a little something like this.
cues.zh: 这观点真是蠢透了，我们稍后会聊到。我甚至记得年轻时看过一篇报道，说加热表面消耗的能量比白炽灯信号灯还多，所以这么折腾到底图啥？这就是“但是偶尔……”思维的危险之处。它的逻辑大概是这样的。

cues.en: The LED stoplight is more energy efficient, costs less to operate, requires less maintenance, can allow for a feasible battery backup solution, lasts longer, are brighter and easier to see, particularly in direct sunlight, but sometimes snow and ice builds up on them, so clearly they are bad. This makes me so disappointed in humanity. When there's a new innovation which changes how we do things for the better, its benefits are obvious.
cues.zh: LED 信号灯更节能、运营成本更低、维护需求更少、还能支持可行的备用电池方案、寿命更长、更亮且更容易看清——尤其是在阳光直射下——“但是偶尔”上面会积雪结冰，所以它们显然是个糟糕的东西。这真让我对人类大失所望。当一项新创新以更好的方式改变我们的生活时，它的好处明明是显而易见的。

cues.en: The LED stoplight is a perfect example. It allows stoplights to better accomplish their rather important task of being visible, makes them more reliable then and with battery backups functionally superior to an incandescent light, and saves municipalities
cues.zh: LED 红绿灯就是一个绝佳的例子。它能让红绿灯更好地完成“清晰可见”这项极其重要的任务，可靠性更高，而且在有备用电池的情况下，性能上超越了传统的白炽灯，还能为市政部门

cues.en: thousands of dollars, with Wisconsin reporting in 2009 that they saved $750,000 in energy costs annually, which isn't even mentioning maintenance costs. However, when the but sometimes rears its ugly head, people tend to freak out. Suddenly, all those benefits go away because in this one particular facet of stoplight functionality, the wasteful and maintenance-heavy incandescent lamp is accidentally superior. Suddenly, when the new solution presents a new problem, all we think about is the problem.
cues.zh: 节省数千美元——威斯康星州在 2009 年就曾报告，他们每年能节省 75 万美元的能源费用，这甚至还没算维护成本。然而，一旦出现哪怕一点负面转折，人们往往就会大惊小怪。转眼间，所有的好处似乎都被抛在脑后，就因为在红绿灯功能的某一个特定方面，耗能又难维护的白炽灯反而意外更具优势。刹那间，只要新方案带来了一个新问题，我们眼里就只剩下这个问题了。

cues.en: Which leads to the truly stupid part of this argument. But sometimes occurs only some of the time. It's a sometimes. Articles that complain about a potential solution requiring more energy, and thus reducing the efficiency of the new LED stoplight, just kinda gloss over the fact that on every day it's not snowing, the issue is completely irrelevant.
cues.zh: 这就引出了这个争论中最荒谬的部分。但这种情况只是偶尔发生。只是偶尔。那些抱怨潜在解决方案会消耗更多能源、从而降低新 LED 红绿灯效率的文章，完全忽略了一个事实：在不下雪的日子里，这个问题根本就不存在。

cues.en: Sure, if we add heaters to the LED module to melt snow, it might need more power, but only when it's snowing, dingus. It wouldn't take too much imagination to enable wireless control of an intersection's stoplights to turn on the heaters while it snows. Even if the lights used a bit more power while the heaters are on, the other 300 days of the year when it's not snowing don't just go away. It doesn't take too much thinking to realize that it's still saving a lot of energy over the long run.
cues.zh: 当然，如果我们给 LED 模块加装加热器来融雪，它可能会耗费更多电力，但笨蛋，那也只有在下雪的时候才需要啊。稍微动动脑子就能想到，完全可以通过无线控制路口的红绿灯，让它们只在下雪时开启加热器。就算开着加热器时灯会多耗一点电，一年中不下雪的其他 300 天又不会凭空消失。稍微想想就能明白，从长远来看，这依然能节省大量能源。

cues.en: And again, the traffic light is not at fault when an accident occurs. All drivers know, or at least should know, that a malfunctioning traffic light means you must stop and proceed with caution. But we trust people so little in remembering this simple procedure that nearly every intersection has a folded up stop sign ready to be deployed when the traffic lights fail. I'm not opposed to that, I think it's a good idea, but in reality it shouldn't be necessary.
cues.zh: 再强调一次，发生事故并不是红绿灯的错。所有司机都知道，或者至少应该知道，红绿灯故障意味着你必须停下，并在确保安全后谨慎通行。但我们对大家能否记住这个简单的规则太没信心了，以至于几乎每个路口都备有折叠式停车标志，随时准备在红绿灯失效时派上用场。我并不反对这样做，我觉得这是个好主意，但在现实中，这本该是没必要的。

cues.en: Also, in personal experience, a snowstorm severe enough to cause buildup on the traffic light lenses is pretty out of the ordinary. I've never personally encountered a traffic light that's completely obscured with snow. I've seen some partially, but never enough to make the signal impossible to distinguish. After all, there are pretty big visors over the lenses, so it's got to be a real blizzard to cause a problem. And really, in those conditions, you should just avoid driving altogether. This isn't to say that the problem doesn't happen, surely it does.
cues.zh: 而且就我个人经历来说，能严重到在红绿灯镜面上积雪的暴风雪是相当少见的。我个人从没遇到过被雪完全挡住的红绿灯。我见过被挡住一部分的，但绝不至于让人完全分辨不出信号。毕竟红绿灯上方有相当大的遮阳罩，所以非得是特大暴风雪才会引发问题。而在那种恶劣天气下，你本来就应该彻底避免开车出门。我并不是说这种情况绝不会发生，它肯定存在。

cues.en: But come on, it's not at all frequent. Now the correct response to the but sometimes is to account for that sometimes and solve the problem. One potential way that doesn't use any energy is through an altered visor with a scoop on top designed to redirect wind to flow across the lens and blow snow off of it. But for those wanting a more high-tech solution, well take a look at this. General Electric now sells what they call GTX FlexLED heated shell.
cues.zh: 但得了吧，这种情况根本就不常见。面对“偶尔会这样”的正确做法，就是把“偶尔”考虑进去并解决问题。有一种完全不耗能的潜在方案，就是改良遮光罩，在顶部加个导流口，引导气风吹过镜面，把雪吹走。但对于想要更高科技方案的人来说，不妨看看这个。通用电气（General Electric）现在推出了他们称为 GTX FlexLED heated shell 的产品。

cues.en: These traffic light modules have defroster wires across their face just like the rear window of your car. What's more, they have sensors on board measuring temperature and humidity to determine when icing conditions are likely and automatically switch on the heaters. The spec sheet says these heaters use only 30 watts, which means even when they are all on, a 3-light traffic light is using less power than a single incandescent bulb. Not much less, but I must remind you that the need for the heater is rare, and only of sometimes.
cues.zh: 这些交通信号灯模块表面装有除霜电热丝，就像你汽车的后车窗一样。更厉害的是，它们内置了测量温度和湿度的传感器，用来判断何时可能结冰，并自动开启加热器。规格表上说这些加热器只消耗 30 瓦，这意味着即使全部开启，一组三色信号灯的功耗也比单个白炽灯泡还要低。虽然没低多少，但我必须提醒你，需要开加热器的情况极少，真的只是“偶尔”。

cues.en: It looks like this is a relatively new product, with the site touting it as new and the copyright date on the spec sheet being 2016. So it seems we got along well enough without this innovation for… a while. Probably because people realized how infrequent the problem actually is. But anyway, the problem's been solved. The but sometimes is now a never. The moral of this story is that when faced with a unique, unforeseen, or difficult problem that comes about as a result of doing things in a different way,
cues.zh: 这看起来是个相对较新的产品，官网上标榜它是新品，规格表上的版权年份也是2016年。所以看来在很长一段时间里……没有这项创新我们也过得挺好的。大概是因为大家意识到，这个问题实际上极少发生。但不管怎样，问题已经解决了。“有时会出现的问题”现在变成了“绝不出现”。这个故事告诉我们，当面对因为用新方式做事而引发的奇特、未预见或棘手的问题时，

cues.en: Don't just give up. It's beyond foolish to fly in the face of progress, especially when the result of the progress is so obviously better, just because there's a tiny little sometimes maybe issue that we haven't had before. I'll bet you no municipality that has switched to LED traffic signals wants to go back to the old way of doing things. But that's what news articles and media coverage like this seem to advocate for. Now obviously I don't want us to not acknowledge problems. That would be silly. But when discussing these problems, we need to look at them from all sides.
cues.zh: 不要轻言放弃。仅仅因为出现了一个以前从未有过的、极其微小且偶尔可能发生的问题，就去公然抗拒进步，这简直蠢到家了，尤其是当这种进步带来的结果明显要好得多的时候。我敢打赌，换了LED交通信号灯的市政部门，没有哪个想退回到过去的老路子上。但类似的新闻文章和媒体报道似乎就在鼓吹这种倒退。当然，我显然不是说要去无视问题，那样做太蠢了。但在讨论这些问题时，我们需要从各个角度全面来看。

cues.en: Just how bad is the problem, really? How often does it occur? What would we be giving up if we abandoned our efforts, and should we abandon them? What can we do to combat the problem? Does the problem need a technical fix, or do we need to re-educate people and adjust their behavior? Perhaps the problem isn't so much a problem, rather it's a need for change elsewhere. But for goodness sake, we need to work to solve the problem. Every innovation has changed how we do things in some way,
cues.zh: 这个问题到底有多严重？它发生的频率有多高？如果我们放弃努力会失去什么，我们又该不该放弃？我们能做些什么来应对这个问题？它是需要技术手段来修复，还是需要重新教育大家并调整人们的行为？也许这个问题本身并不算什么大问题，而是其他地方需要做出改变。但无论如何，我们都必须努力去解决它。每一项创新都在某种程度上改变了我们做事的方式，

cues.en: That's the very idea of progress. Sometimes this change brings new issues to light and may bring inconveniences from time to time. But I don't think this should be seen as a reason to stop progress. I hope that as new technologies and innovations become available, that provide us advantages just as the LED traffic light has, that we don't simply focus on the new problems they might create. Together, we should be asking how to solve those new problems. When we ask that question and work towards the answers,
cues.zh: 这正是进步的本质所在。有时这种改变会暴露出新的问题，也可能会时不时带来一些不便。但我认为，这绝不该成为阻碍进步的理由。我希望，随着像 LED 交通灯这样能带来优势的新技术和新创新不断涌现，我们不要只盯着它们可能带来的新问题。我们应该共同探讨如何解决这些新问题。当我们提出这个问题并为之寻找答案时，

cues.en: we can truly make progress. Okay, so there's some other stuff I want to bring up real quick. First, I'm officially launching my second channel. Head on over to Technology Connections 2 if you'd like to see what's on the inside of one of these LED modules. I've always been a little curious. Don't, uh, don't go over just yet. There's, okay, here's a card, but the end screen will have it too, and there's a link down below. One thing that I've noticed change about traffic light behavior is the timing of the right turn arrow.
cues.zh: 我们才能真正取得进步。好了，我还有些别的事想简单提一下。首先，我的二副频道正式开通了。如果你想看看这些 LED 模块内部长什么样，不妨去 Technology Connections 2 看看。我一直都对此挺好奇的。呃，先别急着走。这里，好的，这里有个卡片，片尾画面也会有，下方也有链接。关于交通灯的变化，我注意到的有一点就是右转箭头的亮灯时机。

cues.en: I realize this whole video has been from the perspective of the US, where we drive on the right and our traffic signals look like… well, like that and all the other things you've been seeing in the video. So maybe this isn't a thing in other countries and honestly this could be a regional thing within the US. But at intersections where there are both left turn only and right turn only lanes, the right turn lane will typically get a green arrow while the opposing traffic gets a protected left, because no one will be coming from the left hand side going straight across.
cues.zh: 我意识到整个视频都是基于美国的视角，我们靠右行驶，交通信号灯长成……呃，长成那样，还有视频里看到的其他各种情况。所以这在其他国家可能并不常见，老实说甚至在美国本土也可能有地域差异。但只要十字路口同时设有左转和右转专用道，通常在对向车流获得专用左转绿灯时，右转车道也会亮起绿色箭头，因为左侧不会有直行车辆穿过来。

cues.en: It used to be very common for the green arrow to light up as soon as the yellow light appeared, which was great because it meant if you were turning right, you knew that you could just proceed even though forward traffic was about to stop. Most intersections these days seem to wait until the opposing traffic gets their protected left before illuminating the right turn arrow, which means you need to stop before you actually get the arrow.
cues.zh: 过去很常见的情况是，直行黄灯一亮，右转绿箭头就跟着亮起，这招特别好用，意味着哪怕直行车流马上要停，准备右转的你也知道自己可以直接开过去。不过如今大多数路口似乎都要等到对向车流真正拿到专用左转信号后，才会亮起右转箭头，这就意味着你在箭头真正亮起之前，还是得先停下来。

cues.en: I suppose this might be a safety thing, but really, I can't see how much safer it is because pedestrians would not be entering the intersection at all while there's a protected left because vehicles will be crossing their path no matter which direction they're going. And it's really annoying in this age of distracted driving because some drivers see the light turn red, come to a stop, and then look at their phones without realizing there's a turn arrow now illuminated. If the arrow were already lit, they could have just kept going and annoyed someone elsewhere.
cues.zh: 我想这可能是出于安全考虑，但老实说，我实在看不出能安全多少，因为在专用左转信号亮起时，行人们根本不会穿过路口，毕竟不管车往哪个方向开都会横切他们的路线。而在如今开车容易分心的时代，这就特别烦人了，因为有些司机看到红灯停下后，就开始看手机，压根没注意到转弯箭头其实已经亮了。如果箭头早早就亮着，他们本来可以直接开走，去别处惹人烦了。

cues.en: Going back to my particular town situation, there's one intersection near me that's an absolute hodgepodge of stuff. Almost nothing matches anymore in this intersection. There are individual LED retrofits among incandescent lights, such as this pair of signals where there is only one LED signal among the 10 total lights. But most amusingly, the pedestrian signals are almost all completely different.
cues.zh: 回到我所住的小镇情况，我家附近有个路口简直是大杂烩。这个路口里的设备几乎没一样是统一配套的。白炽灯里混杂着个别改装的 LED 灯，比如这一对信号灯，在总共 10 个灯头里竟然只有一个是 LED 的。但最搞笑的是，人行横道信号灯几乎全都长得完全不一样。

cues.en: There are still some old written walk-don't-walk signs combined into a single fixture. Then there's the newer pictographic signals with the talk to the hand and the walking white guy. Then there's an LED version of the same thing with two distinct shapes. And then there's an LED signal where the shapes are combined. And finally, there's one that has a countdown timer.
cues.zh: 现在还有一些老式的文字“通行-禁行”信号灯，都整合在一个灯具里。然后是较新的图形信号灯，带有“红手禁行”和“白人步行”图标。接着是同一款式的 LED 版本，分成两个独立的图案。再往后是图案重叠合一的 LED 信号灯。最后，还有一种带有倒计时读秒的。

cues.en: That strikes me as particularly odd because it means the controller for this intersection is capable of driving a countdown timer, so clearly it has been updated within the last decade or two, but there are some comparatively ancient fixtures here. I realize this style of light where there are multiple diodes right at the face that fail over time is kind of an old style at this point. Most newer traffic lights are like these, where they are designed to mimic how incandescent fixtures look. In fact, GE calls these incandescent look. That's part of why I want to check out the innards of one of these.
cues.zh: 这让我觉得特别奇怪，因为这意味着该路口的控制器是支持倒计时的，显然在过去一二十年里更新过，但这里却保留着一些相当古老的灯具。我也意识到，这种表面密布多个二极管、时间一长就会坏掉的信号灯，放到现在确实算老款式了。现在多数较新的交通灯都像这样，专门设计成模仿白炽灯的外观。事实上，GE 就管这类叫“仿白炽灯外观”。这也是我想拆开看看其中内部构造的原因之一。

cues.en: I doubt there's a single 10 watt LED chip in here, so I would imagine they also don't necessarily fail altogether, but it would be a lot harder to see if it's failing at a glance. I glossed over the vehicle presence detection a little bit and just showed what it looks like, and sometimes this isn't even visible. Generally, there will be a loop of wire embedded below the road surface that's designed- Really?
cues.zh: 我怀疑这里面用并不是单颗 10 瓦的 LED 芯片，所以我猜它们大概率也不会直接全坏掉，但一眼看上去就很难看出是不是出故障了。我刚才对车辆感应检测一笔带过，只是展示了它的样子，而且有时它甚至都是看不见的。通常路面下会埋有一圈感应线圈，专门用来——真的吗？

cues.en: I glossed over the vehicle presence detection a little bit and just showed what it looks like, and sometimes this isn't even visible. Generally, there will be loops of wire embedded below the road surface that are designed to detect a change in their magnetic field brought about by a large metal object above them, such as a vehicle. You can often see these, particularly if they were added to an already existing road surface.
cues.zh: 我刚才对车辆感应检测一笔带过，只是展示了它的样子，而且有时它甚至都是看不见的。通常路面下会埋有一些感应线圈，用来检测上方像车辆这样的大型金属物体所引起的磁场变化。你经常能看到这些线圈，尤其是在现有路面上后期加装的情况。

cues.en: Sometimes, you'll notice them way far back from the intersection, and by adding them here, the traffic control system can count how many vehicles are approaching, and thus how much time is needed for them to cross the intersection. There's some pretty clever thought going into all these systems. Oh, and sometimes you'll see cameras up where the traffic signals are, and some of these are used for presence detection using computer vision. Also, the emergency vehicle detectors are a pretty neat thing that perhaps you know how they work, but I'll tell you anyway. I said tuned strobe light earlier.
cues.zh: 有时你会注意到它们离路口非常远，装在那是为了让交通控制系统计算有多少车辆正在接近，从而算出它们通过路口需要多少时间。这些系统中蕴含着不少精巧的设计。哦对了，有时你还会看到红绿灯处装有摄像头，其中一些是用计算机视觉来进行存在检测的。此外，应急车辆检测器也是个挺绝的玩意儿，或许你已经知道它的工作原理了，但我还是要讲讲。我刚才提到了“特定频率的频闪灯”。

cues.en: What I mean by that is that emergency vehicles have a single white strobe light, often in the center of their light bars, which flashes at a very specific frequency. It's often hard to see on video because strobe lights and video just don't really get along, but it's this one here on this ambulance. The traffic light controller is looking for a signal at that specific frequency coming from the photo cells up top, and when it sees it, it will begin stopping traffic.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，应急车辆上通常在警灯正中央有一盏单独的白色频闪灯，它会以非常特定的频率闪烁。这在视频里通常很难看清，因为频闪灯和视频拍摄总是犯冲，但救护车上的就是这盏。交通灯控制器会通过顶部的光敏元件寻找该特定频率的信号，一旦识别到，就会开始拦截其他车流。

cues.en: These white indicators are used to confirm to the driver of the emergency vehicle that the signal was received and that opposing traffic is being stopped. In Illinois, where I live, the lights will flash in the direction the emergency vehicle is coming from, and they will illuminate steadily for opposing traffic to warn them an emergency vehicle is coming. Interestingly, this isn't really taught in driver's ed, and the lights don't have any sort of sign to explain their purpose, but hopefully enough people have figured this out to make them useful.
cues.zh: 这些白色指示灯用来向应急车辆驾驶员确认信号已被接收，对向车流正在被拦截。在我居住的伊利诺伊州，应急车辆驶来方向的指示灯会闪烁，而对向车流方向的指示灯则会长亮，提醒他们有应急车辆正在靠近。有趣的是，驾校其实并不教这个，灯旁边也没有任何标牌解释其用途，但希望有足够多的人明白这一点，让它们发挥作用。

cues.en: Lastly, for those towns who like the charm of these old 8 inch stoplight fixtures, you'll be happy to know that GE and probably others too make LED retrofits for these. Thanks for your consideration.
cues.zh: 最后，对于那些钟情于老式8英寸红绿灯外壳魅力的城镇，你们会很高兴地得知，GE以及其他厂商都生产了适配这种灯具的LED改装套件。所以赶快跟上时代吧，各位。感谢收看，希望大家喜欢这期视频。如果你是第一次看到这个频道，请考虑订阅。一如既往地非常感谢Patreon上的支持者们。正是你们的支持让这些视频得以不断更新。如果你也有兴趣支持本频道，请去我的Patreon页面看看。感谢大家的关注与支持。

cues.zh: 好的，所以如果可以的话，去看看 Technology Connections 2 吧，如果你能顺手点个订阅就太棒了。随着时间推移，我会在那边发布更多额外内容。我们下期再见。
